keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the topic (Korea is not the only place where people celebrate the night with light) and the conclusion (festivals of light all share one message of hope). The green sentences are the answers.

qs.q: Why did people long ago love light so much?
qs.qko: 옛날 사람들이 빛을 그토록 좋아한 이유는 무엇인가요?
opts: Because darkness meant cold and danger, while light meant warmth and safety
Because light helped them grow rice faster
Because they wanted to scare away elephants
evs: For thousands of years, darkness meant cold, danger, and fear, while light meant warmth, safety, and hope.
This is Yeondeunghoe, the Lotus Lantern Festival held before Buddha's Birthday.
Jewish families light one more candle each night for the eight nights of Hanukkah.
People in very different places came to the same idea without ever meeting each other.
why: 수천 년 동안 어둠은 추위·위험·두려움을, 빛은 따뜻함·안전·희망을 뜻했다고 했어요.
For thousands of years, darkness meant cold, danger, and fear, while light meant warmth, safety, and hope.

qs.q: In "People in very different places came to the same idea," what does "came to" mean?
qs.qko: «People in very different places came to the same idea» 에서 «came to» 는 무슨 뜻인가요?
evs: People in very different places came to the same idea without ever meeting each other.
But Korea is not the only place where people celebrate the night with light.
Why do so many different cultures love festivals of light?
Suddenly, thousands of glowing lanterns float past you, shaped like lotus flowers, dragons, and elephants.
why: 서로 만난 적도 없는데 같은 생각을 하게 되었다고 했어요. 그러니 «came to» 는 어떤 생각에 «이르다, 떠올리게 되다» 라는 뜻이에요.
They never met, but they all had the same idea, so «came to» means they thought of or reached that idea.

qs.q: Why do many light festivals happen when the nights are longest?
qs.qko: 많은 빛 축제가 밤이 가장 긴 때에 열리는 이유는 무엇인가요?
opts: Because people want light and hope during long, dark nights
Because lanterns are cheaper in winter
Because rivers are warmer in winter
evs: Here is a clue: many of these festivals happen in autumn or winter, when the nights are longest.
In India, families light rows of small clay oil lamps for Diwali.
For thousands of years, darkness meant cold, danger, and fear, while light meant warmth, safety, and hope.
This is Yeondeunghoe, the Lotus Lantern Festival held before Buddha's Birthday.
why: 많은 빛 축제가 밤이 가장 긴 가을이나 겨울에 열리고, 사람들에게 빛은 따뜻함과 안전과 희망을 뜻했어요. 두 문장을 이으면 긴 밤에 빛이 더 필요했다는 걸 알 수 있어요.
Many light festivals happen when the nights are longest, and light meant warmth, safety, and hope. Together, they show people wanted light most during long, dark nights.
